title: Quality and appropriateness of the researcher's professional experience, competences and skills
content:
## 1.4 Quality and Appropriateness of the Researcher's Professional Experience, Competences and Skills

### Spine-dependency notice

The fellow's identity — name, current institutional affiliation, country of origin, PhD institution and year, complete publication record, citation history, full career stage documentation, and any personal statement of motivation — carries status Unresolved (token: FELLOW; confirmation_checklist.json; still_requires_real_confirmation: true). No source vault node names any fellow. The vault records only an inferred PI Role (METH-PART-003, Inferred) from first-person authorship of the design narrative and attributed ownership of a peer-reviewed calibration method (doi:10.1016/j.envsoft.2022.105556; concept_note.md, source_grounded reference to 'the fellow-attributed method'), but the person's name and institutional affiliation are explicitly absent from every vault node. The confirmation checklist records the attribution question as open: 'A PI Role is INFERRED from first-person authorship of the design narrative and ownership of the calibration method; whether that person is the PF fellow or the PF supervisor is itself open' (confirmation_checklist.json, FELLOW, what_source_says). For structural coherence only, the synthetic working spine (SYN-SPINE-01, working_assumptions.json; §3 operator override, logged in decision_log/synthetic-spine-demo-override_2026-07-13.json) supplies a placeholder: [FELLOW — Unresolved; synthetic working value: Dr. Mariya Petrova, postdoctoral researcher, Plovdiv University 'Paisii Hilendarski', Bulgaria; SYNTHETIC, not real, not submittable]. Every statement about the researcher's personal attributes, career history, affiliation, and CV data in this sub-section that draws on the synthetic spine is flagged accordingly and must be replaced with operator-confirmed facts — including a formal Part B-2 curriculum vitae and list of publications — before any submission is finalised. The structural competence analysis and the appropriateness argument presented below are derived from the project's research architecture and can be validated against the confirmed CV; they do not depend on accepting any synthetic identity claim.

### The evaluator's frame for this sub-criterion

Sub-criterion 1.4 addresses a specific question within the MSCA-PF Excellence criterion (50% weight; call_analysis_summary.json, source_grounded from ef_he-msca_en.pdf): whether the researcher's existing professional experience, competences and skills are of high quality and appropriate to the proposed research project. SR-01 (scope_requirements.json, Confirmed, mandatory) frames the fellowship instrument as being 'provided to excellent researchers undertaking international mobility' — excellence of the researcher is not peripheral context but the instrument's central individual-level selection criterion. The evaluator's task is to assess whether the documented track record prior to the fellowship makes that characterisation credible for this specific project. An excellent generic researcher poorly matched to the specific research design is a weak case; a well-matched researcher whose overall track record is thin is equally weak. Quality and appropriateness are jointly required and neither suffices alone.

For this project, appropriateness has an unusually concrete technical meaning. The research architecture couples four disciplines — Earth observation remote sensing, probabilistic machine learning, crop physiology and agricultural hydrology, and agricultural economics — across three pipeline stages: multi-sensor probabilistic fusion (OBJ-1, WP1), uncertainty-aware crop simulation (OBJ-2, WP2), and economically rationalised irrigation decision under uncertainty (OBJ-2, WP2). A researcher who has already demonstrated technical mastery of the most demanding discipline-specific competence at one of these stages — the competence hardest to build from scratch in a 24-month fellowship [DURATION — Unresolved, confirmation_checklist.json; operator-declared 24 months under SYN-SPINE-01] — is the most appropriate entry profile for this specific design. The source record provides one inference-grade piece of evidence that exactly this condition may be met, grounded in the calibration method referenced in concept_note.md. That evidence is not yet confirmed by identity documentation.

### What the source record establishes: the PI Role inference and the prior calibration method

The only research-substance evidence about the researcher in the source vault is a single peer-reviewed calibration method: doi:10.1016/j.envsoft.2022.105556 (concept_note.md, source_grounded, referenced as 'the fellow-attributed method building on which OBJ-2 is designed'; PI Role inference, METH-PART-003, Inferred from first-person authorship of the design narrative). This attribution is Inferred, not Confirmed, because the vault names no author — the inference derives from the design narrative's first-person voice and from the technical ownership implied by describing the calibration approach in first-person terms. The same caveat recorded in confirmation_checklist.json must be carried forward into the appropriateness argument: whether the method's author is the fellowship's fellow or its supervisor, or a third party, is an open question. The attribution of the prior method to the fellow rather than the supervisor is the hinge on which the entire appropriateness case for sub-criterion 1.4 turns, and it requires confirmation before the evaluator can accept the case as made.

Subject to confirmed attribution: the calibration method (doi:10.1016/j.envsoft.2022.105556) establishes uncertainty-aware AquaCrop calibration retaining an explicit parameter posterior rather than converging to a single best-fit parameter set (METH-DEC-002, source_grounded, concept_note.md). This is the direct technical prerequisite for OBJ-2 (objectives.json, Confirmed, source_grounded; vault nodes METH-DEC-001, METH-DEC-002). The decision engine at the core of OBJ-2 cannot propagate uncertainty through the AquaCrop model interface without retaining a parameter posterior: standard deterministic AquaCrop calibration minimises a loss function to produce one parameter set, which is then held fixed, introducing no parameter uncertainty into subsequent simulations and effectively breaking the uncertainty chain (METH-CORE-004, source_grounded) at the soil-water-plant interface. The prior method solved exactly this problem for a deterministic field-state input — single known entry conditions entering the calibration — demonstrating that the calibration step can be performed while maintaining honest uncertainty without collapsing to an overconfident point estimate. The fellowship extends this demonstrated capability in two directions that together constitute the project's scientific advancement. Upstream, the input to calibration becomes an uncertain field-state posterior from the probabilistic fusion model (WP1, OBJ-1, objectives.json, Confirmed), rather than a deterministic known state — requiring the calibration to propagate input-state uncertainty into the parameter posterior rather than treating the state as given. Downstream, the calibration's combined parameter-and-state uncertainty propagates through counterfactual irrigation simulation over weather ensembles (METH-DEC-003, METH-DEC-004, source_grounded, concept_note.md) into the profit-maximising recommendation (METH-DEC-005, METH-DEC-006, source_grounded, concept_note.md). The fellowship is thus a specific, architecturally coherent extension of a demonstrated prior capability — not a change of research direction, not an application of a generic skill to a new domain, but a targeted upstream and downstream closure of a chain whose central demonstrated node is the prior method itself. The scientific continuity is unusually strong for a postdoctoral fellowship: the work the fellowship aims to produce is methodologically entailed by the work already demonstrated, not merely related to it.

The specificity of fit between the prior method and the project's architectural requirement constitutes the appropriateness argument's strongest confirmable element. Uncertainty-aware calibration of AquaCrop is not a generic modelling skill. AquaCrop's parameter space — encoding soil-water-plant dynamics, canopy development functions, root deepening rates, biomass water productivity coefficients, and water stress response curves — is agronomy-specific and requires both probabilistic inference methodology and crop-science parameter semantics to calibrate in a posterior-retaining way. A probabilistic ML practitioner without crop-science grounding will misspecify priors over physiological quantities. An agronomist without probabilistic ML grounding will default to point-estimate calibration. The prior method demonstrates the simultaneous command of both, which is the specific competence combination required by T2-01 (WP2; wp_structure.json, Confirmed). A researcher who brings this specific prior demonstration to the fellowship enters OBJ-2 not at the frontier of their capability but extending a demonstrated technical achievement — a structurally different and more credible appropriateness case than one built on projected capacity development.

### Disciplinary competence profile mapped to project requirements

The project requires four disciplines at the four coupling points of the observation-to-decision pipeline. Sub-section 1.2 established the structural necessity of this interdisciplinarity and is not repeated here; the present analysis maps the researcher's inferred entry-profile competences against each discipline's specific role in the project to assess the appropriateness of the match at each stage.

**Probabilistic machine learning for environmental inference — direct competence (Inferred from prior method, METH-PART-003).** The prior calibration method demonstrates probabilistic ML applied to a mechanistic environmental model: specifying prior distributions over physiological and soil-hydraulic quantities, designing a likelihood function connecting model outputs to observed yield and phenology data, implementing an efficient posterior inference algorithm, and diagnosing calibration quality. These are canonical probabilistic ML tasks applied to the environmental domain, and their prior peer-reviewed demonstration is the researcher's strongest confirmed technical asset. This competence is directly required by the fellowship's most technically demanding task: T1-02 (WP1, implement probabilistic fusion model Route A/B; wp_structure.json, Confirmed) requires exactly the ability to specify probabilistic models over latent environmental quantities and perform posterior inference. The model families named in the concept — Bayesian hierarchical models and Gaussian processes (concept_note.md, source_grounded) — are the two most established probabilistic ML model families for spatial environmental inference, and a researcher with prior posterior-inference experience in the AquaCrop calibration context brings directly transferable methodology to the fusion problem. The extension from calibrating a mechanistic model's parameters to estimating a latent field state from multi-sensor covariates is a change in the object of inference, not in the inferential methodology; the probabilistic ML competence transfers directly.

**Crop physiology and agricultural hydrology — adjacent competence embedded in prior method (Inferred from prior method domain, METH-PART-003).** Calibrating AquaCrop while retaining a posterior requires agronomic knowledge of which parameters are most uncertain given available calibration data, what their plausible ranges are from agronomic literature, and how parameter uncertainty interacts with the soil-water-plant dynamics AquaCrop encodes. This domain knowledge is embedded in the prior calibration approach and is not separable from the probabilistic inference methodology: an ill-specified agronomic prior produces an ill-calibrated posterior regardless of the sophistication of the inference algorithm. The researcher thus brings crop-physiology competence not as a separately claimed research area but as a jointly embedded dimension of the demonstrated calibration capability. This competence is directly required by OBJ-1's latent field-state definition (root-zone soil moisture, crop water stress, canopy condition; objectives.json, Confirmed, source_grounded) and by T2-01's AquaCrop parameter prior specification task (WP2; wp_structure.json, Confirmed). Specifying an informative prior over AquaCrop's water stress response functions without crop-physiology background produces an uninformative or misspecified prior, undermining the uncertainty chain at its central calibration stage.

**Earth observation remote sensing and satellite data engineering — adjacent competence requiring fellowship-scale development.** The prior method's established domain is crop simulation calibration, not multi-sensor EO fusion. The extension to heterogeneous multi-sensor EO data in OBJ-1 — Sentinel-1 SAR, Sentinel-2 optical, optional PlanetScope, soil sensors, and weather data (objectives.json, Confirmed, source_grounded; METH-INFRA-002, source_grounded) — involves EO data engineering competences not self-evidently demonstrated by the prior calibration method: atmospheric correction, cloud masking for optical gaps compensated by SAR (RISK-03, Inferred, risks.json), geometric co-registration across sensor geometries, and temporal compositing across heterogeneous overpass cycles. The fellowship's WP1 (T1-01 'Acquire and harmonise EO and ground sensor data', T1-02, T1-03; wp_structure.json, Confirmed) is specifically structured to develop and consolidate this EO competence in combination with the researcher's existing probabilistic ML foundation. Whether the researcher brings prior EO data engineering experience beyond the calibration method is an open factual question: the source vault records no EO data publication or demonstrated satellite data processing capability, and the confirmed CV must supply this evidence. If EO data engineering is a genuine entry-profile gap, the transition from the prior method's deterministic field-state input to Route A's one-step probabilistic fusion of heterogeneous EO data (METH-ROUTE-001, source_grounded, concept_note.md) represents a substantial technical development step. This risk is acknowledged and mitigated by two design features: the Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 data the project uses are freely available ESA Copernicus open data requiring no access negotiation (METH-INFRA-002, source_grounded, concept_note.md), meaning the EO data engineering challenge is a competence development task rather than an access negotiation task; and Route B (METH-ROUTE-002, source_grounded, concept_note.md) sidesteps the sub-pixel EO fusion complexity by selecting a nearby spectrally homogeneous patch the coarse satellite pixel reads cleanly, providing a fallback diagnostic route with lower EO data engineering demands that still exercises the full downstream uncertainty chain. The two-route architecture is therefore partly a risk-management strategy for the EO competence development risk: Route B reduces the minimum EO data engineering requirement, preserving OBJ-1's achievability even if Route A's one-step fusion implementation takes longer than planned.

**Agricultural economics — partial competence requiring fellowship-scale development.** The profit-based decision objective (METH-DEC-005, METH-DEC-006, source_grounded, concept_note.md) frames irrigation recommendation as expected-profit maximisation — expected crop value minus full irrigation costs — across the weather ensemble. The researcher's prior AquaCrop calibration context addresses the simulation component of this decision chain but does not demonstrate prior command of agricultural economic objective function specification or farm-scale economic optimisation. Whether the researcher brings agricultural economics training or prior engagement with decision-theoretic frameworks for farm management is not evidenced in the vault. T2-02 (WP2, 'Build counterfactual irrigation simulation and decision engine'; wp_structure.json, Confirmed) provides the structured research context for developing this competence within the fellowship: the economic objective function (RQ6, Confirmed as open, confirmation_checklist.json; default framing: expected crop value minus costs) is explicitly held open, allowing the researcher to specify its form during the fellowship at the point where they have developed sufficient agricultural economics competence to make an informed choice. This design flexibility in RQ6 is itself a mechanism for reducing the entry-profile requirement in this discipline: the researcher does not need to bring fully formed agricultural economics expertise from day one but must develop a working command of economic decision criteria within the 24-month working scaffold by month 15 (MS3, milestones_seed.json, Confirmed). The inter-sectoral engagement with the validation partner [VALIDATION_PARTNER — Unresolved; confirmation_checklist.json] during WP3 field validation — when farming practitioners communicate their actual operational irrigation decision constraints — provides the real-world economic grounding that complements the formal decision-theory framework.

The competence mapping has a clear structural logic that justifies the fellowship design. The researcher's demonstrated prior capability anchors the most technically demanding and discipline-specific stage of the pipeline, which is also the stage most difficult to develop from scratch within the fellowship duration. The two disciplines requiring the most fellowship-scale development — EO data engineering and agricultural economics — are the disciplines where the project's own design provides the most risk-managed pathways: Route B reduces EO complexity if Route A exceeds capacity, and RQ6's open specification defers the agricultural economics commitment until the researcher has developed working competence. This is the appropriate match between researcher entry profile, project design, and fellowship training architecture.

### Career stage, professional independence, and the fellowship's positioning objective

MSCA Postdoctoral Fellowships target experienced researchers at the postdoctoral career stage — researchers who hold a doctoral degree at the time of the submission deadline (2026-09-09; selected_call.json, CALL_BINDING Confirmed, confirmation_checklist.json) or have at least four years of full-time equivalent research experience since PhD. The researcher's role is recorded as 'Experienced researcher / postdoctoral fellow (the applicant)' in project_summary.json (spine_marker: SYN-SPINE-01, Confirmed-synthetic). Whether the real researcher satisfies this eligibility criterion — specifically, whether they hold a doctoral degree or have at least four years of full-time research experience by the submission deadline — is Unresolved (FELLOW, confirmation_checklist.json) and must be documented in the confirmed Part B-2 curriculum vitae.

One dimension of professional independence is addressable from the vault without confirmed identity: the design narrative of the project demonstrates intellectual ownership at a level consistent with an independently thinking researcher who has moved beyond implementing established methods to designing novel frameworks. The choice to treat the uncertainty chain (METH-CORE-004, source_grounded, concept_note.md) as an architectural invariant rather than a convenient design feature — and to frame its empirical falsifiability rather than its expected success as the validation protocol's core commitment — reflects a research voice with epistemological clarity about what honest uncertainty quantification requires and what it cannot claim. The explicit maintenance of ten open scientific decisions (RQ1–RQ10, confirmation_checklist.json, all Confirmed as open) rather than asserting resolved answers reflects an active researcher who distinguishes between design commitments that can be made from existing knowledge and research questions that must be answered by the fellowship's empirical programme. These stylistic and epistemological properties of the design narrative are consistent with an advanced postdoctoral researcher transitioning toward independent research leadership — but they are inferential observations about the design narrative, not confirmed CV evidence.

The strategic positioning (strategic_positioning.md, Tier 3) characterises the fellowship as advancing the fellow 'from postdoctoral researcher toward independent research leadership', with the Career Development Plan (D4-01, due month 3; SR-07, scope_requirements.json, Confirmed; T4-01, WP4; wp_structure.json, Confirmed) specifying the individual career trajectory jointly with the supervisor. Measurable career advancement targets — at minimum three peer-reviewed publications (at minimum two first-authored), co-supervision of at minimum one MSc thesis, and a follow-on national or ERC-track proposal submitted within six months of the fellowship's end — are OBJ-5 scaffold values (objectives.json; evidence_strength: unconfirmed; spine_marker: SYN-SPINE-01, spine-dependent) and cannot be calibrated against the real researcher's existing publication count and trajectory until the confirmed CV is available. The evaluator's assessment of whether these targets are ambitious but achievable relative to the researcher's established record is entirely dependent on the confirmed CV. A researcher with no first-authored publications who proposes two first-authored publications over 24 months is making an ambitious claim that requires strong explanation; a researcher with an established first-author record who proposes the same increment is proposing a realistic continuation. This calibration requires confirmed data that is currently absent.

### International mobility, the mobility rule, and fellowship type determination

SR-01 (scope_requirements.json, Confirmed, mandatory) positions the fellowship instrument as requiring excellent researchers undertaking international mobility. SR-02 (scope_requirements.json, Confirmed, mandatory) specifies that a European Fellowship must take place in an EU Member State or Horizon Europe Associated Country and that the researcher must satisfy the MSCA mobility rule: no more than 12 months' residence or main activity in the host country in the 36 months immediately preceding the submission deadline (2026-09-09). Both determinations — the researcher's country of origin and the host's country — are Unresolved because FELLOW and HOST are Unresolved (confirmation_checklist.json).

On the synthetic working spine (SYN-SPINE-01), the fellowship is a European Fellowship derived from an intra-EU move: the fellow moves from Plovdiv University 'Paisii Hilendarski' (Bulgaria; EU Member State) to Eötvös Loránd University ELTE (Budapest, Hungary; EU Member State). This intra-EU mobility makes the fellowship a European Fellowship by definition under SR-02 (scope_requirements.json, Confirmed). FELLOWSHIP_TYPE is Unresolved (confirmation_checklist.json; still_requires_real_confirmation: true) because the EF determination rests entirely on the synthetic host. If the real host is in a non-associated Third Country, the fellowship type becomes a Global Fellowship under SR-03 (scope_requirements.json, Confirmed), requiring a mandatory 12-month return phase, constraining eligibility to European nationals or long-term residents, and changing the knowledge-transfer model from two-way to three-way. These downstream implications are architecturally consequential: the research programme designed on a 24-month EF scaffold (milestones_seed.json; wp_structure.json) would require restructuring for a 24–36-month GF scaffold with an outgoing phase and a return phase. FELLOWSHIP_TYPE is one of the two most consequential Unresolved items for proposal structure.

The MSCA mobility rule itself — the 12-months-in-36-months ceiling on prior residence or main activity in the host country — cannot be verified from current Tier 3 data and must be checked against the confirmed researcher's actual residence and employment record for the 36-month window ending on 2026-09-09. No proxy inference from the synthetic spine's country-of-origin (Bulgaria) serves as verification: the mobility rule applies to the confirmed host country and the confirmed researcher's actual prior residency record, not to a synthetic pairing. A researcher with Bulgarian nationality who spent two years as a visiting researcher or employed at the confirmed host institution in Hungary (or in whatever country the confirmed host is in) may fail the mobility rule despite the apparent cross-country move.

The international mobility dimension of sub-criterion 1.4 contributes to expected outcome EO-02 (New mind-sets and approaches to R&I work forged through international, inter-sectoral and interdisciplinary experience; Confirmed, expected_outcomes.json; Inferred mapping, concept_refinement_summary.json). The proposed mobility creates the conditions for interdisciplinary immersion — the researcher's probabilistic ML and crop-physiology background entering the host's environmental-physics and geoinformatics environment — that EO-02 describes as the mechanism through which new mind-sets are forged. Whether the real mobility produces an analogous disciplinary immersion effect depends on the confirmed host's actual research environment, which is Unresolved (HOST, confirmation_checklist.json).

### Scientific motivation as a dimension of professional profile

The fellowship's research motivation, as expressed in the design narrative (concept_note.md, source_grounded), rests on two converging elements that together constitute a scientifically coherent motivation rather than a claimed opportunity: a literature-evidenced gap and a demonstrated technical capability that partially closes it. The gap is the research-gap matrix's empty cell (METH-SOTA-006, source_grounded, concept_note.md) — real-time irrigation decision support combined with high-resolution imagery — documented as the least-covered combination in a systematic review of approximately 50 studies (METH-SOTA-001, source_grounded, concept_note.md). The capability is the prior uncertainty-aware AquaCrop calibration method (doi:10.1016/j.envsoft.2022.105556, Inferred attribution), which demonstrates command of the specific probabilistic modelling technique required at the pipeline's middle stage. The convergence of a documented literature gap at the end of the pipeline and a demonstrated capability at its middle creates a specific, testable scientific question: whether maintaining uncertainty honestly throughout the full observation-to-decision chain produces more trustworthy irrigation recommendations than collapsing to point estimates at each coupling step. This question is scientifically motivating precisely because the answer might be negative — uncertainty might fail the calibration test (RISK-06, Inferred, risks.json), Route B covariation might not hold (RISK-05, Inferred, risks.json), Route A might exceed available computational resources (RISK-07, Inferred, risks.json) — and the design explicitly accommodates these negative outcomes by framing them as scientifically valid findings rather than project failures. A research motivation that only makes sense if the answer is positive is a marketing case; this motivation is structurally valid whether the answer is positive or negative, which reflects a professional scientific orientation that is appropriate for a fellowship targeting independent research leadership.

The quality of the scientific motivation as a dimension of the researcher's professional profile cannot be fully assessed from the design narrative alone. Evaluators will also consider the researcher's personal statement of motivation — a document absent from all current Tier 3 data — and any letters of support or reference letters that speak to the researcher's intellectual engagement with the problem domain. These documents cannot be substituted by the vault-derived motivation analysis above.

### Confirmed strengths and irreducible gaps: summary assessment for evaluators

The following table summarises what is confirmable about the researcher's appropriateness from current Tier 3 data and what requires confirmed CV data before the sub-criterion can be scored:

**Confirmable from vault inference (subject to attribution confirmation):**
— The prior calibration method (doi:10.1016/j.envsoft.2022.105556) demonstrates uncertainty-aware AquaCrop calibration retaining a parameter posterior: the direct technical prerequisite for OBJ-2's most demanding task (T2-01, WP2; Inferred attribution, METH-PART-003).
— The appropriateness of this prior competence to the project's central technical challenge is unusually specific: it is not a generic modelling skill claimed to be relevant, but the exact prior demonstration of the exact technique required at OBJ-2's central task.
— The probabilistic ML competence embedded in the prior calibration method transfers directly to the Route A probabilistic fusion model required by T1-02 (WP1), reducing the entry-profile gap in the project's most methodologically novel contribution.
— The crop-physiology competence embedded in the prior calibration method covers OBJ-1's field-state specification requirements, reducing the disciplinary gap at OBJ-1.
— The design narrative's epistemological clarity, explicit management of open scientific decisions, and honest calibration of what the project can and cannot claim are consistent with the professional independence indicators appropriate for an advanced postdoctoral researcher (Inferred from design narrative, METH-PART-003 PI Role inference).
— The two disciplines requiring the most fellowship-scale development (EO data engineering; agricultural economics) are each addressed by structural design features that reduce the minimum entry-profile requirement: Route B reduces EO complexity; RQ6's open specification defers the agricultural economics commitment.

**Irreducible gaps requiring confirmed CV data before sub-criterion 1.4 can be scored:**
— The attribution of the prior calibration method to the fellow rather than the supervisor or a third party must be confirmed. This is the single most consequential gap in the appropriateness case: the entire OBJ-2 competence-fit argument rests on it.
— The researcher's complete publication record (number, quality, citation profile, journal impact profile, first-authorship ratio) must be documented in the Part B-2 CV. The vault references one method publication; whether this is one of many or the only one is unknown.
— Career chronology (PhD institution, discipline, year; postdoctoral positions; gap analysis if any) must be established to verify eligibility and assess career stage appropriateness.
— Prior project leadership and independent grant history must be documented to support the 'transition to independent research leadership' characterisation.
— EO data engineering experience, if any, must be confirmed from the CV to assess the Route A implementation risk relative to the Route B fallback.
— Agricultural economics background, if any, must be confirmed to calibrate the scope of RQ6 development required within the fellowship.
— MSCA mobility rule compliance must be verified against the confirmed researcher's actual 36-month residence and employment record.
— FELLOW eligibility criterion (doctoral degree or four years of FTE research experience by 2026-09-09) must be confirmed.

The evaluator's score for sub-criterion 1.4 will ultimately be determined by the confirmed researcher's actual publication record, career trajectory, and CV as documented in Part B-2, not by the structural competence fit analysed in this sub-section. That fit is — subject to attribution confirmation — as strong as any researcher in the reviewed literature could offer for this specific project design. Whether the researcher's overall record meets the quality standard MSCA-PF targets for this career stage is the question the confirmed CV must answer, and it is a question this sub-section cannot answer in the absence of that document.
